title: Chest discomfort after lunch
learner_confidence_target: I can act safely before I know everything.

visible_station_card.candidate_information: You are the doctor in a general practice clinic. David Nguyen, 58 years old, has booked an urgent same-day appointment because of chest discomfort after lunch.

prompts: What serious cause must stay on my radar?
Which details would make this unsafe to manage routinely?
At what point must assessment become urgent action?

guided_run.label: Guided real run
guided_run.description: A realistic consultation with a short safe reasoning guide beside each clinical turn.
guided_run.interaction_rule: One clinical beat. One spoken response. One continue action.

beats.title: Open and test the label

cue.speaker: David Nguyen
cue.text: Doctor, I think it is just indigestion, but my chest feels really tight.

safe_reasoning_guide: He thinks it is indigestion. That may be true.
But chest pressure can also be serious.
A heart cause is not ruled out.
First, clarify the pain pattern.
beats.doctor_line: David, I can see you are uncomfortable. I understand why you thought it might be indigestion. I am going to ask a few focused questions to make sure this is not something more serious.
beats.learner_instruction: Say the opening aloud in your own words.

beats.title: Clarify the pain pattern

cue.speaker: David Nguyen
cue.text: It started about 45 minutes ago while I was carrying boxes. It is a heavy, tight pressure in the middle of my chest, about 8 out of 10. It goes to my left arm and jaw, and it is still there. The antacid did not help.

safe_reasoning_guide: This started with effort.
It is heavy, central and spreads to the arm and jaw.
Simple indigestion is now less reassuring.
A heart problem is more concerning.
Next, check sweating, nausea, breathlessness and fainting.
beats.doctor_line: Did you feel sweaty or sick? Have you been short of breath, dizzy or faint?

beats.title: Recognise the safety threshold

cue.speaker: David Nguyen
cue.text: I am sweaty, I feel sick in the stomach, and I am a bit short of breath. I have not fainted.

safe_reasoning_guide: Sweating, nausea and breathlessness add to the concern.
This is still not a proven diagnosis.
But it is unsafe to keep this as a routine clinic assessment.
Arrange urgent ambulance transfer now.
Keep checking him while help is coming.
beats.doctor_line: David, these symptoms could be coming from your heart. I am arranging an ambulance now while I continue checking you.
beats.learner_instruction: Explain the concern and urgent action aloud.
candidate_actions: Ask staff to call an ambulance now.
Keep David in the clinic and stay with him.
Use an ECG only if it is immediately available and does not delay transfer.
Do not wait for clinic blood tests or troponin.

beats.title: Hold the safety boundary

cue.speaker: David Nguyen
cue.text: An ambulance? Is it that serious? Can I just drive myself? I have an important work meeting, and I do not want to make a fuss.

safe_reasoning_guide: He does not yet understand the risk.
His wish to drive creates another safety problem.
Stay calm. Do not argue.
Explain why monitored transport matters.
Keep the boundary clear.
beats.doctor_line: I understand the meeting matters, but I do not want you to drive because your condition could change suddenly. The ambulance team can monitor you and start treatment if needed.
beats.learner_instruction: Explain why private driving is unsafe.

beats.title: Assess while transfer is underway

cue.speaker: Examiner
cue.text: David agrees to ambulance transfer and asks you to tell his wife. The ambulance has been called. You continue a focused assessment while waiting.

groups.label: Observations
items: Pale, sweaty and uncomfortable
HR 104
RR 22
SpO₂ 95% on room air
Temperature 36.8°C

groups.label: Risk and medicines
items: Smokes about 15 cigarettes daily
Hypertension and high cholesterol
Father had a heart attack
Takes blood pressure and cholesterol medicines, sometimes misses doses
No known drug allergy

groups.label: Focused danger checks
items: No tearing pain to the back or syncope
No haemoptysis, calf swelling, recent surgery, long travel or immobilisation
No focal weakness or speech trouble
No fever, cough, chest injury or wheeze
Chest examination: no wheeze or focal crackles
Cardiovascular examination: no new murmur reported

safe_reasoning_guide: The urgent action is already underway.
Now gather only information that changes immediate care or handover.
Check observations, risk factors, medicines, allergies and a few other dangerous causes.
Do not let these checks delay transfer.
beats.doctor_line: While help is coming, I will check your observations, medical history, medicines, allergies and a few other serious causes so I can hand over safely.
beats.learner_instruction: Say how you will continue the focused assessment.
candidate_actions: Check aspirin allergy, active bleeding or ulcer, and relevant anticoagulant use before aspirin.
Check blood pressure and recent PDE5-inhibitor use before GTN.
Give oxygen only if he is hypoxic.

beats.title: Handover clearly

cue.speaker: Examiner
cue.text: The ambulance team arrives. Give a concise clinical handover.

safe_reasoning_guide: The team needs the pattern, the main danger, what you have done and what still needs checking.
Keep the handover short and ordered.
Do not retell the whole consultation.
beats.doctor_line: David Nguyen is 58 with 45 minutes of central heavy chest pressure, 8 out of 10, starting with exertion and radiating to his left arm and jaw, with sweating, nausea and shortness of breath. Antacid did not help. He has smoking, hypertension, cholesterol and family-history risk. I am concerned about possible acute coronary syndrome. Ambulance transfer has been arranged and he has been advised not to drive.
beats.learner_instruction: Give the handover aloud, then finish the station.

blind_repeat.label: Blind repeat
blind_repeat.description: Patient and examiner cues only. The safe reasoning guide and doctor lines are hidden.

review.note: This is self-review guidance, not an automatic score.

core_stages.title: How safe was my run?
items: I did not accept indigestion as the diagnosis.
I recognised the danger pattern after the associated symptoms.
I arranged ambulance transfer before completing the full history.
I clearly stopped private driving.
I continued only focused assessment while help was coming.
I gave a short, ordered handover.

core_stages.title: How the road changed
core_stages.purpose: See what changed, what remained uncertain and why the next safe move changed.

timeline.what_changed: Nothing dangerous had been ruled out.

timeline.moment: Exertional, heavy pressure with arm and jaw radiation
timeline.what_changed: A heart cause became more concerning.
timeline.uncertainty: The diagnosis was still not proven.

timeline.what_changed: The pattern became unsafe for routine clinic assessment.
Communication became part of immediate safety.
timeline.uncertainty: He had not yet accepted the risk.
timeline.next_safe_move: Explain monitored transport and hold the no-driving boundary.

timeline.uncertainty: Other causes and treatment details still needed assessment.
timeline.next_safe_move: Gather only focused information for immediate care and handover.

core_stages.title: See it, practise it, repeat
core_stages.purpose: Use the full run, repair one weak part, then test yourself without prompts.

weak_drills.title: Explain urgent transfer
weak_drills.prompt: David says: An ambulance? I thought it was indigestion.
weak_drills.model: Indigestion is possible, but your symptoms are not safe to treat that way here. The pressure, radiation, sweating, nausea and breathlessness could mean your heart is at risk. I am arranging an ambulance now so you can be monitored and treated safely.

weak_drills.title: Hold the no-driving boundary
weak_drills.prompt: David says: Can I just drive myself? I have a meeting.
weak_drills.model: I understand the meeting matters, but I do not want you to drive because your condition could change suddenly. The ambulance team can monitor you and start treatment if needed.

weak_drills.title: Recover from the indigestion frame
weak_drills.prompt: You initially framed the symptoms as reflux. Change direction safely.
weak_drills.model: I first considered indigestion because this began after lunch. But the heavy pressure, arm and jaw radiation, sweating, nausea and breathlessness make a heart cause unsafe to miss. I need to change direction and arrange urgent transfer.

weak_drills.title: Give a concise handover
weak_drills.model: David Nguyen is 58 with 45 minutes of central heavy chest pressure, 8 out of 10, starting with exertion and radiating to his left arm and jaw, with sweating, nausea and shortness of breath. Antacid did not help. He has smoking, hypertension, cholesterol and family-history risk. I am concerned about possible acute coronary syndrome. Ambulance transfer has been arranged and he has been advised not to drive.

what_if_paths.question: What if I treated it as reflux?
what_if_paths.answer: The danger pattern remains unexplained and the patient may deteriorate without monitoring or urgent assessment.

what_if_paths.question: What if I waited for an ECG?
what_if_paths.answer: An immediate ECG can help, but it must not delay ambulance transfer when the clinical pattern is already high risk.

what_if_paths.question: What if I waited for troponin?
what_if_paths.answer: Troponin is not available in the clinic, and waiting for proof delays safe transfer.

what_if_paths.question: What if I let him drive?
what_if_paths.answer: Private transport is unsafe because the patient may deteriorate suddenly without monitoring or immediate treatment.

what_if_paths.question: What if the ECG was normal?
what_if_paths.answer: A normal early ECG does not make ongoing high-risk symptoms safe in a general practice clinic.

strong_run: Recognises the high-risk pattern before certainty.
Calls an ambulance after the danger threshold is crossed.
Continues focused assessment while transfer is underway.
Explains risk in clear patient language.
unsafe_run: Completes a long routine history before escalating.
Waits for clinic tests or troponin.
Gives protocol medicines without checking contraindications.

immediate_management: Keep David in the clinic and ask staff to assist.
Check observations and obtain an ECG only if it does not delay transfer.
Do not wait for clinic troponin.
Use local suspected-ACS protocol only after contraindication checks.

journey_metadata.confidence_target: I can act safely before I know everything.
